title: Salthouse Lancaster Memorial
crew_summary: 7 killed including Fg Off. William George Corewyn
narrative: Lancaster LM720 of 61 Squadron departed RAF Skellingthorpe on a bombing operation to the Leuna/Merseburg synthetic oil plant in January 1945. Flying Officer William George Corewyn, aged 23, was at the controls when the aircraft struck a 200-foot Type 54 CHEL radar mast on Bard Hill, near Salthouse on the north Norfolk coast, in poor visibility. Misunderstood wireless telegraphy messages are believed to have contributed to the crew's fatal disorientation. All seven men aboard were killed: Corewyn, navigator Flight Sergeant Ronald Charles Battersby, bomb aimer Flight Sergeant Edward James Boakes, flight engineer Sergeant Peter Richard Earl, wireless operator Flight Sergeant Sidney Joseph James, mid-upper gunner Sergeant John Douglas, and rear gunner Sergeant Richard Richardson — the youngest of the crew, aged just 19. The crew are commemorated at St Nicholas' Church in Salthouse, close to where they fell.

crew.name: William George Corewyn
crew.fate_detail: Killed instantly when the Lancaster struck the 200ft radar mast on Bard Hill at 01:21 hours on the return from Leuna.
crew.bio: Pilot serving with the RAFVR, aged 23. Led the crew on a dangerous mission to the heavily defended Leuna synthetic oil complex.

crew.fate_detail: Killed instantly in the collision with the radar mast.

crew.name: Edward James Boakes
crew.fate_detail: Initially survived the crash and was pulled from the wreckage alive but badly injured. Died in hospital at 06:25 hours the same morning.
crew.bio: Bomb aimer serving with the RAFVR, aged 21. The only crew member to initially survive the crash, but succumbed to his injuries in hospital.

memorial_details:
Name: Avro Lancaster LM720
Type: Other memorial
Description: Wall-hung paper scroll mounted on black backboard. Hand-drawn side elevation of Lancaster at top with handwritten dedication and names below. 61 Squadron crest and drawing of Home-Chain radar tower at bottom left.
Inscription: LANCASTER MK III LM720, 61 SQUADRON/SKELLINGTHORPE/ DEDICATED TO THE MEMORY OF THE CREW/ OF THE ABOVE AIRCRAFT WHO DIED/ WHEN IT CRASHED INTO BARD HILL CHEL/ RADAR PYLON RETURNING FROM A RAID / ON MERSEBURG, ON 15TH JANUARY 1945. [crew names inscribed on memorial]
Location: St Nicholas' Church Grouts Lane Salthouse North Norfolk Norfolk NR25 7XQ England
Grid Ref: TG 07621 43682
Coordinates: 52.950323851180,1.089064678768
Photos: https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/132/279/large_nf_salthouse_2.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/132/280/large_nf_salthouse_3.jpg; https://media.iwm.org.uk/ciim5/memorials/132/281/large_nf_salthouse_4.jpg

Memorial Unveiling: The memorial is dedicated to the Avro Lancaster LM720 aircraft and its crew. It commemorates their service during World War II.

Installation of Coast defence No. 1 Mk VI radar (Mid-1943): Bard Hill was equipped with a coast defence No. 1 Mk VI radar mounted on top of a War Office 200' steel tower using the high powered equipment known as the Naval Type 277.

external_narratives.summary: Detailed aircrew memorial page for Fg Off. William G. Corewyn and the crew of Lancaster III LM720 QR:D. Took off at 16:30 from Skellingthorpe for Leuna, Germany, and struck the 200ft CHEL radar mast at Bard Hill at 01:21 on the return. The radar station operators were tracking E-boats when the collision occurred.
key_details: Radar operators were tracking E-boats at time of collision

remembrance.service_description: The crew of this aircraft are remembered at the annual No. 50 & No. 61 Squadrons Association memorial service at Skellingthorpe, near their wartime base. The 2026 service takes place on 7 June — Birchwood memorial at 11:30, village memorial at 14:00.

events.name: 2026 Memorial Service at Skellingthorpe
events.description: Annual service at Birchwood memorial (11:30) and village memorial (14:00). AGM Saturday 6 June at 17:00.

events.name: Commissioning as Coast defence (CD)/Chain Home Low radar station
events.description: Bard Hill was sited on the hill to the south of Salthouse on the north Norfolk coast for this purpose.

events.name: Takeover by RAF
events.description: Bard Hill was included in the first batch of army radar stations used for coast watching to be taken over by the RAF and became immediately operational under its new masters.

events.name: Transition from Chain Home Low (CHL) to Chain Home Extra Low (CHEL)
events.description: German jamming of the CHL rendered the CHL stations less effective. Research allowed a change from metric to centimetric wavelengths, resulting in a pencil beam that was difficult for Germans to jam and enabling the RAF to 'look lower'.

community_connection: The Avro Lancaster LM720 is a memorial dedicated to the crew of a World War II bomber. This memorial likely represents a personal connection or community tribute to the fallen airmen.
